How to use this book

What the book covers, what each box does, who the case companies are, and how this site works with no internet connection.

This book covers every Learning Outcome Statement in CMA Part 1, Section E–F (Internal Controls and Technology), effective September 1, 2024. It is written in graded English (B1+ to B2) with the exact exam terms, and it bridges each term to Arabic.

From the September/October 2026 testing window, English-language CMA exams have 100 multiple-choice questions followed by two case-based questions (CBQs). The Learning Outcome Statements did not change. Every chapter therefore ends with multiple-choice practice and a case-style set in the CBQ format.

Four parts. Part I, Chapters 1 to 5, covers internal controls. Part II, Chapters 6 to 8, covers systems controls and continuity. Part III, Chapters 9 to 12, covers information systems. Part IV, Chapters 13 to 18, covers data analytics.

Each chapter follows the same pattern: an opener figure, learning objectives with LOS codes, key terms, numbered sections, a section check after each section, a chapter summary figure, practice questions, a case question in the official exam format and full answers with explanations.

The case companies

■ U.S. GAAP

Orontes Foods, Inc.

A food and beverage producer based in Amman, Jordan, listed in the United States, so it reports under U.S. GAAP. It makes olive oil and tahini in Amman and frozen pastries in Dubai. Worked through 16 of this book's chapters.

● IFRS

Cedar Retail S.A.L.

The IFRS company. Many countries in the Middle East and North Africa — Jordan and the United Arab Emirates among them — require IFRS for listed companies. Worked through 1 of this book's chapters.

Numbers

Amounts are in whole U.S. dollars unless a table says USD 000, as each one's heading says. Examples that begin with “Suppose” are illustrative: they are not part of a case company's reported statements. Figure and question numbers keep their chapter prefix, for example F411-03.

Where the exam asks you to type an amount, enter it without the $ sign and without commas — for example 1250. The numeric boxes in this site accept answers the same way.

The boxes inside the Brief

Press Brief at the top of any page and these are the boxes you meet inside it. This volume carries 21 of them.

WORKED EXAMPLE

A calculation or analysis, step by step.

How this site works

  • Every screen asks you to decide something. There are no screens that only show you a figure or a statement: the author's figures appear inside the exercise built on them, where you need them, and every screen is marked. This volume has 706 section checks.
  • Press Brief at the top of any page for the explanation. It gives that section in the author's own words, the terms with their Arabic and a speaker for each, one drawing of the mechanism, and a list of what the page asks you to do. It never contains an answer to an exercise on that page.
  • Every exercise has Check Answers and Try Again. Try Again re-shuffles the item and clears your marks — it never reveals the answer as a shortcut.
  • Answers are shuffled every time, and in a matching or sorting exercise there are always more tiles than places to put them, so the last one is never free.
  • Feedback leads with your own choice. When you are wrong, the first thing you read is the reason for the option you picked, taken from the book's own explanations.
  • Every term is bridged to Arabic. Each of the 18 chapters has a term bank that drills its key words both ways, and the glossary and the index of terms gather them all.
  • Drag-and-drop always has a click path. Tap a tile, then tap where it goes. Everything is operable from the keyboard too: Tab to a tile, Enter to pick it up, Tab to a target, Enter to drop.
  • Pronunciation uses your computer's voices. On Windows, Chrome and Microsoft Edge expose the installed voices directly. If an Arabic icon is dimmed, no Arabic voice is installed — Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech → Add voices → Arabic.
  • Progress is saved in this browser on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere. The foot of any chapter page has a button to clear it.
  • No web server, no internet, no install. Open index.html straight from the folder. Press ← and → to move between screens, and use your browser's print command for a clean worksheet of any practice page.

The first part of this book

1 · Control Risk, Objectives and the Control Environment — five numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

2 · Corporate Governance: the Board, the Officers and the Hierarchy — five numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

3 · Control Activities: Segregation of Duties and Safeguarding — six numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

4 · Sarbanes-Oxley, the PCAOB and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act — six numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

5 · COSO, Risk Types, Testing and Remediation — seven numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

Chapters 6 to 18 are built too, from Systems Security: Threats, Access and Segregation to Data Visualization. Every chapter follows the same shape. The number of sections is the book's, not a template's — across this volume it runs from 5 to 7. Each chapter saves its progress separately, so resetting one leaves the others alone.
